# --- 1) Panel A: Module HotNet enrichment dot plot --- #

```{r panel_a_setup}
# --- HotNets --- #

# Define HotNet neighborhood order
hotnet_order <- c(
    "Active zone", "Presynaptic membrane", "Postsynaptic specialization",
    "Presynaptic ion channels", "Postsynaptic organization"
)

# Overall SynGO synapse enrichment is shown alongside the HotNets, in its own facet so it
# reads as a summary column rather than another neighborhood
syngo_label <- "All synaptic"

# Define HotNet domains and create label abbreviations
df_hotnet_domain <- tibble(
    hotnet_group = c(syngo_label, hotnet_order),
    domain       = c(NA, "CC", "CC", "CC", "BP", "BP"),
    prepost      = c("Overall", "Presynaptic", "Presynaptic", "Postsynaptic",
                     "Presynaptic", "Postsynaptic")
) %>%
    mutate(
        hotnet_group_label = str_replace(hotnet_group, "Presynaptic ", "") %>%
            str_replace("Postsynaptic ", ""),
        hotnet_group_label = factor(hotnet_group_label, levels = unique(hotnet_group_label)),
        hotnet_group       = factor(hotnet_group, levels = c(syngo_label, hotnet_order)),
        domain             = factor(domain,  levels = c("CC", "BP")),
        prepost            = factor(prepost, levels = c("Overall", "Presynaptic", "Postsynaptic"))
    )

# Shared aesthetics: ring width encodes significance tier. Ring color is held constant so
# that the color aesthetic is free to carry the odds-ratio legend (see the plot chunk)
sig_stroke_sizes <- c("FDR < 0.05" = 0.5, "p < 0.05" = 0.2)


# --- Modules --- #

# Which synaptic gene set definition is shown (05_00 section 1 computes all three), and
# which programs the panel covers. GR is tested in 05_00 and reported in the supplement,
# but is not part of the synaptic hypothesis this panel addresses
syngo_set_shown   <- "Synapse (CC)"
topic_order_panel <- c("SYN", "MORPH")

# Overall synapse enrichment becomes one more column alongside the HotNets
df_syngo_shown <- df_module_syngo_ora %>%
    filter(gene_set == syngo_set_shown, topic_label %in% topic_order_panel) %>%
    mutate(hotnet_group = syngo_label)

# Modules ordered within topic by the significance of their overall synaptic enrichment,
# so the strongest synaptic modules lead each block
module_order_all <- df_syngo_shown %>%
    mutate(topic_label = factor(topic_label, levels = topic_order_panel)) %>%
    arrange(topic_label, p_value) %>%
    pull(module_label)

# Bold the module label where the module's #1 hub by kME (or the regulon's TF) is itself
# an ASD risk gene
y_label_lookup <- df_stepwise_res %>%
    distinct(module_label, hub_is_risk_gene) %>%
    transmute(module_label = as.character(module_label),
              md = ifelse(hub_is_risk_gene, paste0("<b>", module_label, "</b>"), module_label)) %>%
    deframe()

# Point size encodes -log10(FDR), capped: the overall SynGO test reaches ~1e-96 where the
# HotNet tests bottom out near 1e-7, so uncapped its points would swamp the panel. Odds
# ratio drives fill intensity and spans ~1.3-6.6, so it needs no cap
fdr_cap <- 10

# Fill is precomputed as white -> topic color scaled by odds ratio, rather than mapped
# through alpha, so points stay opaque: panel gridlines do not show through them and the
# significance ring keeps full contrast (same approach as the Fig 2 AUCell panel)
topic_ramps <- map(topic_colors, ~ colorRamp(c("white", .x)))

df_hotnet_ora_plot <- bind_rows(df_module_hotnet_ora, df_syngo_shown) %>%
    filter(topic_label %in% topic_order_panel) %>%
    # depleted sets would plot as faint points, reading as weak enrichment
    filter(p_value < 0.05, fold_enrichment > 1) %>%
    mutate(
        log10_fdr    = pmin(-log10(p_adj), fdr_cap),
        sig_tier     = if_else(p_adj < 0.05, "FDR < 0.05", "p < 0.05"),
        module_label = factor(module_label, levels = module_order_all),
        hotnet_group = factor(hotnet_group, levels = c(syngo_label, hotnet_order)),
        fill_color   = map2_chr(odds_ratio / max(odds_ratio), topic_label,
                                ~ rgb(topic_ramps[[.y]](.x), maxColorValue = 255))
    ) %>%
    # right_join keeps a column for every HotNet, including those with nothing to plot
    right_join(df_hotnet_domain, by = "hotnet_group")

# Separators between topic blocks. Modules with no significant result are dropped from
# the axis, so positions have to come from the modules actually drawn; the y axis is
# reversed, so they are counted up from the bottom
modules_drawn <- intersect(module_order_all, as.character(df_hotnet_ora_plot$module_label))
topics_drawn  <- df_syngo_shown$topic_label[match(modules_drawn, df_syngo_shown$module_label)]
topic_hlines  <- length(modules_drawn) -
    head(cumsum(rle(topics_drawn)$lengths), -1) + 0.5
```

```{r panel_a_stats}
syn <- df_module_syngo_ora %>%
  filter(gene_set == "Synapse (CC)") %>%
  mutate(
    log_or = log(odds_ratio),
    se     = (log(ci_upper) - log(ci_lower)) / (2 * qnorm(0.975))
  ) %>%
  filter(is.finite(log_or), is.finite(se), se > 0,
         topic_label %in% c("SYN", "MORPH", "GR"))


# pooled OR + 95% CI per program (meta-analytic)
syn %>%
  group_by(topic_label) %>%
  group_modify(~{
    m <- rma(yi = .x$log_or, sei = .x$se, method = "REML")
    tibble(k = m$k, OR = exp(m$b[1]),
           CI_lower = exp(m$ci.lb), CI_upper = exp(m$ci.ub),
           p_vs_null = m$pval, I2 = m$I2)
  }) %>% ungroup()



df3 <- syn %>%
  dplyr::filter(topic_label %in% c("SYN", "MORPH", "GR")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(topic_label = factor(topic_label, levels = c("GR", "MORPH", "SYN")))  # GR = reference

m <- rma(yi = log_or, sei = se, mods = ~ topic_label, data = df3, method = "REML")
summary(m)

# effect sizes as OR ratios relative to GR, with CIs and p-values
data.frame(
  term  = rownames(coef(summary(m))),
  ratio = exp(coef(m)),                 # intercept = GR OR; others = MORPH/GR and SYN/GR
  ci_lo = exp(m$ci.lb),
  ci_hi = exp(m$ci.ub),
  p     = m$pval
)
```


```{r plot_module_hotnet_ora, fig.width = 2.5, fig.height = 4}
p_module_hotnet <- df_hotnet_ora_plot %>%
    ggplot(
        aes(x = hotnet_group_label, y = module_label, size = log10_fdr)
    ) +
    geom_point(aes(fill = fill_color, stroke = sig_tier),
               shape = 21, color = "black", na.rm = TRUE) +
    # invisible: exists only to drive the grayscale odds-ratio colorbar, since fill is an
    # identity scale and cannot produce a legend of its own
    geom_point(aes(color = odds_ratio), shape = NA, na.rm = TRUE) +
    # separators between GO topic groups down the module axis
    geom_hline(yintercept = topic_hlines, color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.4) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = ~ str_wrap(.x, width = 12)) +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = rev, labels = y_label_lookup, na.translate = FALSE) +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(1, 3.5), name = "-log10(FDR)",
                          breaks = c(2, 5, 10), labels = c("2", "5", "≥ 10"),
                          guide = guide_legend(nrow = 1)) +
    scale_fill_identity() +
    # points carry their topic color; the key is drawn white -> black so it reads as one
    # odds-ratio scale rather than three
    scale_color_gradientn(colors = c("white", "black"), name = "Odds ratio",
                          na.value = NA,
                          guide = guide_colorbar(barwidth = unit(1.4, "cm"),
                                                 barheight = unit(0.15, "cm"))) +
    # na.translate = FALSE keeps the empty right_join cells out of the legend key
    scale_discrete_manual(aesthetics = "stroke", values = sig_stroke_sizes,
                          name = "Significance", na.translate = FALSE,
                          guide = guide_legend(nrow = 1,
                                               override.aes = list(size = 3, fill = "white",
                                                                   color = "black"))) +
    facet_grid(cols = vars(prepost), scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
         title = "MORPH links transcriptional regulation\nto synaptic localization") +
    theme(
        plot.title            = element_text(size = 7, hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x           = element_text(size = 5, angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, color = "black"),
        axis.text.y           = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 5, color = "black"),
        strip.text            = element_text(size = 6, face = "bold"),
        strip.clip = "off",
        strip.background      = element_blank(),
        legend.position       = "bottom",
        legend.key.size       = unit(0.3, "cm"),
        legend.box            = "horizontal",
        legend.box.spacing    = unit(0.1, "cm"),
        legend.spacing.y      = unit(0.18, "cm"),
        legend.margin         = margin(t = -2, b = 0),
        legend.text           = element_text(size = 5),
        legend.title          = element_text(size = 5),
        legend.title.position = "top",
        panel.border          = element_rect(linewidth = 0.25),
        panel.spacing         = unit(0.15, "cm")
    )

p_module_hotnet
```

# --- 2) Panel B: MORPH subclusters ball-and-stick plot --- #

```{r morph_network, fig.height = 2, fig.width = 5.5}
morph_color <- topic_colors[["MORPH"]]

# --- Data --- #

# Per-gene subcluster assignment (Misc / cluster 4 has no label and is not plotted)
cluster_vec <- df_MORPH_subclusters %>%
    separate_rows(genes, sep = ", ") %>%
    dplyr::select(genes, MORPH_cluster) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    deframe

# Node attributes shared by the MORPH + MEF2C plots: GO topic (fill) + log10(BF) (size)
node_stats <- df_gene_assignments %>%
    mutate(log_bf = log10(BF)) %>%
    dplyr::select(gene_name, GO_topic, log_bf)

# Bold/outline genes: top hub (rank 1 by kME) + TFs of ASD modules
hubs <- df_module_kme %>%
    filter(module == kME_module & module %in% df_stepwise_res$module) %>%
    group_by(module) %>% slice_max(kME, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% pull(gene_name)
tfs <- df_stepwise_res %>%
    filter(study %in% c("Wamsley", "Wang")) %>%
    mutate(module_label = str_remove(module_label, "\\ .*")) %>% pull(module_label)
nodes_to_bold <- c(hubs, tfs)

# Short panel titles
MORPH_short_labels <- c(`1` = "TFs", `2` = "Microtubules", `3` = "Actin & signaling")

# One within-cluster graph per subcluster (go_knn_edges; genes with no edge dropped)
morph_nets <- map(set_names(names(MORPH_short_labels)), function(cn) {
    cl    <- intersect(names(cluster_vec[cluster_vec == cn]), rownames(MORPH_net$sim_mat))
    edges <- go_knn_edges(MORPH_net$sim_mat[cl, cl, drop = FALSE], k_nn = 3) %>%
        filter(similarity > 0)
    graph_from_data_frame(edges, directed = FALSE)
})

# Shared scale limits so the size / edge-width legends are comparable across panels
sim_rng   <- morph_nets %>% map(~ E(.x)$similarity) %>% unlist() %>% range()
logbf_rng <- node_stats %>%
    filter(gene_name %in% unlist(map(morph_nets, ~ V(.x)$name))) %>%
    pull(log_bf) %>% range(na.rm = TRUE)


# --- Plot --- #

# Per-panel padding + layout seed (tuned so node spacing reads evenly across panels)
xmult_by_cluster <- c(`1` = 0.15, `2` = 0.10, `3` = 0.10)
ymult_by_cluster <- c(`1` = 0.05, `2` = 0.30, `3` = 0.30)
seed_by_cluster  <- c(`1` = 1221, `2` = 1214, `3` = 0916)

morph_plots <- imap(morph_nets, ~ plot_go_graph(
    net = .x, node_stats = node_stats, bold_genes = nodes_to_bold,
    title = MORPH_short_labels[[.y]], size_range = c(1, 4),
    size_limits = logbf_rng, edge_limits = sim_rng,
    seed = seed_by_cluster[[.y]], xmult = xmult_by_cluster[[.y]], ymult = ymult_by_cluster[[.y]]
))

# Combine: three subclusters in a row, widths proportional to gene count (TFs widest)
p_morph <- wrap_plots(morph_plots, guides = "collect") +
    plot_layout(widths = c(3, 0.75, 1))
p_morph
```


# --- 3) Panel C: ASD TF regulon GO similarity plot ---

```{r asd_tf_network, fig.height = 5, fig.width = 4}
# Regulons shown in panels C and D. Every regulon with an ASD risk gene as its TF is
# available in asd_tf_regulon_nets / df_syngo_res (see 05_02); list here the ones to plot
regulons_to_plot <- c("MEF2C_+_+", "SOX11_+_+")

regulon_labels <- df_stepwise_res %>%
    filter(module %in% regulons_to_plot) %>%
    dplyr::select(module, module_label) %>%
    deframe()

# Regulon TF symbol, taken from the module name (e.g. MEF2C_+_+ -> MEF2C)
regulon_tfs <- set_names(str_remove(regulons_to_plot, "_.*"), regulons_to_plot)

asd_risk_genes <- df_asd_rarevar_zscore %>%
    filter(FDR < 0.001 & !FLAG) %>%
    pull(gene_name) %>%
    unique()

# One GO-similarity graph per regulon, over its ASD risk genes, each node linked to its
# top-3 non-zero-similarity partners (go_knn_edges). Vertices are supplied explicitly so
# that risk genes with no GO annotation still appear, as isolated nodes
regulon_graphs <- map(set_names(regulons_to_plot), function(mod) {
    risk  <- intersect(rownames(asd_tf_regulon_nets[[mod]]$sim_mat), asd_risk_genes)
    edges <- go_knn_edges(asd_tf_regulon_nets[[mod]]$sim_mat[risk, risk], k_nn = 3) %>%
        filter(similarity > 0)
    graph_from_data_frame(edges, directed = FALSE, vertices = tibble(name = risk))
})

# Shared scale limits so node size and edge width mean the same thing in every panel.
# Named separately from the panel B ranges so re-running this chunk cannot clobber them
regulon_sim_rng   <- regulon_graphs %>% map(~ E(.x)$similarity) %>% unlist() %>% range()
regulon_logbf_rng <- node_stats %>%
    filter(gene_name %in% unlist(map(regulon_graphs, ~ V(.x)$name))) %>%
    pull(log_bf) %>% range(na.rm = TRUE)

# Only the TF is bolded; larger node size range than the GR / MORPH subclusters. The
# GO-topic fill legend is drawn once, on the first panel: panels differ in which topics
# they contain, so their fill scales are not identical and patchwork cannot merge them
regulon_go_plots <- imap(regulon_graphs, function(g, mod) {
    tf <- regulon_tfs[[mod]]
    plot_go_graph(
        net          = g,
        # the regulon's own TF is drawn black rather than in its GO topic color, so it
        # reads as the driver of the regulon rather than one more member of it
        node_stats   = node_stats %>%
            mutate(GO_topic = if_else(gene_name == tf, "TF", GO_topic)),
        fill_values  = c(topic_colors, "TF" = "black"),
        bold_genes   = tf,
        title        = paste0("ASD genes in the ", regulon_labels[[mod]], " regulon"),
        size_range   = c(2, 6),
        size_limits  = regulon_logbf_rng,
        # two keys only (smallest and largest node), so the legend stays compact. Rounded
        # inward: a break outside the scale limits is silently dropped from the legend
        size_breaks  = c(50, 125),
        edge_limits  = regulon_sim_rng,
        topic_legend = (mod == regulons_to_plot[1]),
        seed         = 1221,
        xmult        = 0.05,
        ymult        = 0.05
    )
})

p_regulon_go <- wrap_plots(regulon_go_plots, ncol = 1, guides = "collect") &
    theme(
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.box = "horizontal",
        legend.direction = "vertical",
        legend.title.position = "top"
    )
p_regulon_go
```


# --- 4) Panel D:  ASD TF regulon SynGO enrichment ---

```{r asd_tf_syngo, fig.height = 3.5, fig.width = 2.5}
# Top 3 SynGO terms per ontology domain, for each regulon being plotted
df_syngo_plot <- df_syngo_res %>%
    filter(module %in% regulons_to_plot) %>%
    group_by(module, domain) %>%
    slice_min(order_by = p_adj, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(odds_ratio = if_else(
        !is.finite(odds_ratio),
        ceiling(max(odds_ratio[is.finite(odds_ratio)], na.rm = TRUE)),
        odds_ratio
    ))

# Consensus GO topic per regulon, so panel D fills each in its own program color
regulon_topics <- df_module_syngo_ora %>%
    filter(module %in% regulons_to_plot) %>%
    distinct(module, topic_label) %>%
    deframe()

# Bars are filled white -> the regulon's topic color by odds ratio
or_limits <- range(df_syngo_plot$odds_ratio[is.finite(df_syngo_plot$odds_ratio)])
n_or_bins <- 4
or_breaks <- exp(seq(log(or_limits[1]), log(or_limits[2]), length.out = n_or_bins + 1))
# pin the outer edges: exp(log(x)) drifts a hair below x, which drops the largest odds
# ratio out of the top bin and silently returns NA
or_breaks[c(1, length(or_breaks))] <- or_limits

df_syngo_plot <- df_syngo_plot %>%
    mutate(
        or_bin     = cut(odds_ratio, breaks = or_breaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE),
        fill_color = map2_chr((or_bin - 0.5) / n_or_bins, module,
                              ~ rgb(topic_ramps[[ regulon_topics[[.y]] ]](.x), maxColorValue = 255))
    )

# One panel per regulon
plot_regulon_syngo <- function(mod) {
    df_syngo_plot %>%
    filter(module == mod) %>%
    mutate(term = str_remove(term, "\\(.*") %>% str_trim()) %>%

    ggplot(aes(x = -log10(p_adj),
               y = reorder_within(str_wrap(term, 30), -p_adj, domain))) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = fill_color), linewidth = 0.25, width = 0.65, color = "gray80") +
    # invisible: exists only to drive the grayscale odds-ratio colorbar, since fill is an
    # identity scale and cannot produce a legend of its own
    geom_point(aes(color = odds_ratio), shape = NA) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = -log10(0.05), lty = 2, color = "darkgrey") +
    facet_wrap(vars(domain), scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", ncol = 1,
               strip.position = "right") +
    scale_y_reordered() +
    scale_fill_identity() +
    # stepped key, using the same log-spaced bin edges as the bar fills
    scale_color_stepsn(
        colors    = c("white", "black"),
        name      = "Odds ratio",
        transform = "log10",
        limits    = or_limits,
        breaks    = or_breaks[-c(1, length(or_breaks))],
        # formatted on the scale rather than by rounding the breaks, so that the limits
        # printed by show.limits are rounded too
        labels    = label_number(accuracy = 0.1),
        # show.limits labels the ends of the bar; without it the top and bottom of the
        # range are unlabeled and only the interior bin edges are shown
        guide     = guide_coloursteps(barwidth = unit(0.15, "cm"), barheight = unit(1.2, "cm"),
                                      show.limits = TRUE)
    ) +
    guides(size = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) +
    labs(x = "-log10(FDR)", y = NULL,
         title = paste0(regulon_labels[[mod]])) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    theme(
        panel.spacing         = unit(0.1, "cm"),
        panel.border          = element_blank(),
        strip.background      = element_blank(),
        strip.text            = element_text(size = 7, margin = margin(t = 1, b = 1)),
        axis.line             = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.125),
        axis.text.x           = element_text(size = 5),
        axis.text.y           = element_text(size = 5.5),
        axis.title.x          = element_text(size = 6),
        legend.position       = "right",
        legend.title.position = "top",
        legend.box            = "vertical",
        legend.box.just       = "center",
        legend.key.width      = unit(0.15, "cm"),
        legend.key.height     = unit(0.3, "cm"),
        legend.margin         = margin(l = -7),
        legend.spacing        = unit(0.25, "cm"),
        legend.title          = element_text(size = 6),
        legend.text           = element_text(size = 5),
        plot.margin           = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
        plot.title            = element_text(size = 7, face = "bold")
    )
}

regulon_syngo_plots <- map(set_names(regulons_to_plot), plot_regulon_syngo)

p_regulon_syngo <- wrap_plots(regulon_syngo_plots, ncol = 1, guides = "collect")
p_regulon_syngo
```


# --- 5) Combine panels for Fig 4 --- #

```{r combine_fig, fig.height = 9, fig.width = 7.09}
row_top <- p_module_hotnet + wrap_elements(full = p_morph) +
    plot_layout(widths = c(1, 3))

row_bottom <- wrap_elements(full = p_regulon_go) +  wrap_elements(full = p_regulon_syngo) +
    plot_layout(widths = c(1.5, 1))

fig5_combined <- row_top / row_bottom +
    plot_layout(heights = c(1, 3)) &
    plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
    theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10))

fig5_combined

ggsave(
    filename = file.path(figures_dir, "Fig5", "Fig5_raw.pdf"),
    plot = fig5_combined,
    height    = 9,
    width     = 7.09,
    dpi       = 300
)
```
